sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The path was not smooth: revenue fell 6.8% in FY2020, was flat at 0.2% growth in FY2023, then rose 125.9% in FY2024, 114.2% in FY2025 and 65.5% in FY2026 [D130][D284][D338][D393][D448].
The FY2024 step change came from Data Center revenue up 217%, driven by Hopper GPU shipments for LLM training and inference [P22][P23].
FY2026 growth was again data center compute and networking, with Blackwell the majority of Data Center revenue [P10].
Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue and contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% growth [D620][D622][D448].
Within it, Data Center computing grew 59% on Blackwell demand and networking grew 142% on NVLink for GB200 and GB300 systems [P8].
Compute & Networking segment revenue rose 66.5% and contributed 59.2pp, while Graphics contributed 6.2pp [D740][D741][D748].
Operating income grew 60.1% against 65.5% revenue growth, so the incremental operating margin was 57.3% [D449][D448][D475].
Diluted EPS grew 66.7%, slightly ahead of 64.7% net income growth, as the diluted share count fell 1.2% [D452][D450][D470].
Operating margin was 60.4% in FY2026, against a window median of 32.8%, a high of 62.4% in FY2025 and a low of 15.7% in FY2023 [F50][D813][D812][D811].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp to 71.1%, the main drag on operating margin, partly offset by R&D and SG&A leverage of 1.3pp and 0.6pp [D462][F30][D478][D479].
The FY2026 gross-margin decline reflects a $4.5 billion H20 excess inventory and purchase-obligation charge in the first quarter [P7].
Operating expenses rose 40.7%, driven by compensation and compute and infrastructure costs [D468][P9].
Net margin held at 55.6% despite the operating-margin drop, helped by $11.1 billion of other income from unrealized equity gains [F70][X120][P3].
Operating cash flow was $102.7 billion and free cash flow $96.7 billion in FY2026, a 44.8% free-cash-flow margin [F100][F110][D432].
Operating cash flow was 0.86x net income, and free cash flow was 0.81x net income, at the low end of its 0.81x to 0.91x window [D435][D436][D826][D827].
Capex rose 86.7% to $6.0 billion, 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A [D455][F105][D431][D437].
Investing outflows of $52.2 billion were driven by higher equity securities purchases and a non-exclusive license agreement with Groq [F120][P1].
Net cash fell to $2.1 billion, 1.0% of revenue, from $34.7 billion a year earlier, as cash and investments dropped 75.5% to $10.6 billion [D441][D442][D386][D439][D471].
That still ranks at the 83rd percentile of net cash to revenue against six semis peers, whose median is -13.9% [D844][D845].
Buybacks and dividends of $41.1 billion absorbed 42.5% of free cash flow, and long-term debt fell 11.7% to $7.5 billion [D443][D444][F200][D459].
Return on average equity was 101.5%, against a peer median of 20.3% [D447][D849].
Customer concentration is high: one direct customer was 22% of FY2026 revenue and another 14%, both mainly Compute & Networking [P6].
China revenue fell 21.4% in FY2026 and its share dropped to 9.1% from 19.2%, a 4.1pp drag on growth [D545][D544][D541][D546].
The Graphics segment's 25% revenue decline in FY2023 [D754] was a one-period event, with Graphics revenue up 57.0% in FY2026 [D747].
Product revenue members sum to 190% of consolidated revenue in FY2026, so segment figures should not be added together [R2].
If gross margin falls below the FY2026 level of 71.1% in the FY2027 10-K, the inventory-charge pattern would be repeating rather than one-off [F30].
A further decline in net cash below the FY2026 $2.1 billion would signal that buybacks and investments are outrunning cash generation [D441].
Watch whether Data Center's share of revenue holds above the FY2026 89.7%, or Networking's 141.5% growth slows, in the FY2027 10-K [D620][D635].
